conviction_note: The evidence points both ways and none of it is a sourced number the market has not seen. On the negative side: PNC's NII missed its own guide on the deposit-mix and spread drivers Truist already cited, and the September Fed hike works against Truist's receive-fixed swaps, which is a risk to the Q4 guide. On the positive side: a mid-quarter reaffirmation, a $1M open-market buy by the new CEO and an accretive auto-loan exit. So p_up is 50 and the scaled number is 0. impact_sum (-0.2) is the sum of the small findings and is not fitted to it. abs_move is 3.5, above the name's 1.79% median reaction and below the 6.14% event-implied move, which looks rich against seven prints with a 5.94% maximum. It is lifted for the first print under a new CEO, strategic-action noise in the GAAP figures and a likely forward-NII guide.
bar: Company guide for 3Q26 from the 2Q26 release and call (2026-07-17): revenue up ~1% q/q on $5.27B (about $5.32B), TE NII up ~1.5% on $3.667B (about $3.72B), noninterest income ~flat on $1.644B, expense up ~2% to ~$3.1B. FY26 guide: NII +1-1.5% (cut from 2-3%), revenue +3.5-4%, fees ~+10%, expense +1.75%, NCO ~55bp, buyback $5B. https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-truist-beats-q2-2026-eps-but-shares-slip-premarket-93CH-4798511 and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000092230/000009223026000096/ex991-pr2q26.htm. Reaffirmed 2026-09-15 as 'unchanged excluding impact of strategic actions' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000092230/000009223026000105/ex991slide.htm). The EPS consensus is DISPUTED: $1.05 from 16 analysts with a range of $0.37-$1.52, down 5.4% in 30 days (Alphastreet, https://news.alphastreet.com/truist-financial-q3-2026-earnings-preview-october-16-street-expects-1-05-eps/), $1.07 (Benzinga) and $1.13 (Chartmill / Benzinga forecast page). The width of that range almost certainly reflects whether analysts include the RAC reserve recapture and the securities-repositioning loss. Revenue consensus is $5.31-5.42B. Revenue is sized against the company guide; nothing is sized against EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 27.7M shares, 2.3% of float and 3.3 days to cover (Equibles, about 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/TFC); Benzinga showed 2.1% around 2026-09-17. That is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +7.97 vol points (downside paid) with put/call OI of 1.68. The event-implied move is 6.14% against a median reaction of 1.79% over 7 prints. Spot is 46.53: -3.96% over 20 days, -16.6% from the 52-week high, about -12.6% since the $53.25 close before the Q2 print, and below the CEO's $48.36 buy on 2026-09-17. The stock was $46.45 on 2026-10-02, so the slide happened in September and the price has been flat in October. Analysts downgraded heavily in July (Morgan Stanley, UBS, BofA, JPMorgan to neutral/equal weight); the consensus rating is Hold.

findings.finding: PNC reported 3Q26 on 2026-10-15. NII rose $99M (+2.4%) to $4.21B against its own guide of +3% to 3.5%, even though average loans grew 2.5%, above its +1-2% guide. The interest-bearing deposit rate rose 7bp to 1.98%, which PNC called mix-driven. Noninterest-bearing deposits fell 2% q/q to 22% of deposits, loan spreads fell about 3bp and NIM fell 2bp to 2.94%. Those are the same three drivers (deposit mix, NIB migration, loan-spread compression) behind Truist's July cut of its FY NII guide to +1-1.5% and its Q3 guide of +~1.5%. Add the mid-September 25bp Fed hike, a baseline of two more hikes, and Truist's CFO saying the receive-fixed swap book weighs as SOFR rises (peaking around 1Q27). The guide at risk is mainly Q4 / early-2027 NII, more than the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-17 Truist cut its FY NII guide from 2-3% to 1-1.5% while beating EPS ($1.23 against $1.08); the stock moved -1.41% on the session and has fallen about 12% since. Its biggest reaction in the baseline (+5.94% on 2025-01-17) and the +3.67% on 2025-10-17 were not traced to a line. A guide cut on this name has been worth about -1.5 points on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: PNC printed this morning, a month after Truist last spoke (Barclays, 2026-09-15), so Truist's consensus NII has had no time to absorb it. PNC's own stock barely moved (+0.66% premarket), which suggests the market did not treat the NII shortfall as an industry signal. If it were fully priced into TFC, TFC would have dropped today. It has not: spot of 46.53 matches the 10-02 level. Against that, the put skew (+7.97) and the -12.6% since the July guide cut already price a large part of this direction, so the finding is sized small.
findings.independence: Separate sources: PNC's 2Q26 slide guide of NII +3-3.5% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026048308/a2q26earningsslides_vf.htm); PNC call commentary on the mix-driven +7bp deposit cost and the -3bp spread (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-pnc-beats-q3-2026-profit-view-as-revenue-slips-93CH-4952250); Fed hike in September and long yields at multi-year highs (AP/Fortune 2026-10-13, https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/); Truist's own CFO on swap pressure as SOFR moves and the NIB mix falling to ~25% (Q2 call, https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-truist-beats-q2-2026-eps-but-shares-slip-premarket-93CH-4798511). Counter-evidence: the same CFO said higher medium and long rates help fixed-rate asset repricing, and PNC still projects Q4 NIM at 3% or more. It is a peer proxy, not a Truist number.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-15 (8-K Item 7.01, Barclays conference), Truist said its 3Q26 and FY2026 outlook was 'unchanged excluding impact of strategic actions' and its $5B 2026 buyback target was unchanged. That was 2.5 months into the quarter, so management had seen most of Q3 NII, fees and expense when it reaffirmed a quarter-on-quarter guide of NII +1.5%, fees flat and expense +2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (EPS $1.09 against about $1.00) moved +2.31% and Q2 2026 (EPS $1.23 against $1.08) moved -1.41%. Reported-quarter beats on this name have not reliably paid, and the reaction followed the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is public and inside the guide. What may not be priced is the asymmetry. The EPS consensus fell 5.4% in 30 days and the put skew is +7.97, which looks like the market leaning toward a Q3 miss that management, with 10 of 13 weeks seen, did not flag. If the market believed the reaffirmation, the skew would be flatter and the consensus would not be drifting down.
findings.independence: Same document as the RAC-sale finding below; this finding uses only the outlook line. Consensus drift from Alphastreet (https://news.alphastreet.com/truist-financial-q3-2026-earnings-preview-october-16-street-expects-1-05-eps/). Nothing independent confirms the Q3 numbers.

findings.finding: Truist signed an agreement to sell substantially all of Regional Acceptance Corp's assets (about $5.5B of near-prime auto loans; buyer reported by Bloomberg as Apollo), expected to close late Q3 or early Q4. Terms: $5.2B net proceeds, a $535M loan-loss reserve recapture and +$945M (22bp) of CET1. It plans to reposition AFS securities to fully offset that capital and to repay wholesale borrowings. RAC was about breakeven pre-tax in H1 2026, the sale cuts NCOs about 10bp a year, and management guides 'modest' 2027 EPS and ROTCE accretion. 3Q26 or 4Q26 GAAP will carry a provision benefit and a realised securities loss. A repositioning done with long yields at multi-year highs reinvests at higher yields, which supports the forward NII guide that includes strategic actions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history in the baseline. In the 2024 securities repositioning (a large realised AFS loss with an NII pickup) the market looked through the GAAP loss to the NII accretion. That case is not in this baseline and is noted only as context.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public, so most of it is priced. What may be mispriced is the EPS bar: estimates range from $0.37 to $1.52 on a $1.05 mean (Alphastreet), which means some analysts include the repositioning loss or the reserve recapture and some do not. A headline GAAP EPS that looks like a miss or a beat could move the open, and how much NII the repositioning adds, quantified in the forward guide, is not modelled on any page found. The stock fell from the CEO's $48.36 buy price after the announcement rather than rising, so no accretion is in the price.
findings.independence: Banking Dive (https://www.bankingdive.com/news/truist-exit-near-prime-auto-lending-sell-5b-loans/830392/) and American Banker (https://www.americanbanker.com/news/under-new-ceo-truist-is-exiting-near-prime-auto-lending) report the same terms; RBC's Cassidy expects more divestitures. Both rest on the same 8-K, so they count once.

findings.finding: New CEO Mike Lyons (CEO since 2026-09-01) bought 21,000 TFC shares in the open market on 2026-09-17 at an average of $48.36 (about $1.01M), two days after the RAC exit was announced and a month before his first earnings print. Spot is now 46.53, 3.8% below his price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy episodes are in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public through the Form 4, but the stock fell after the buy instead of rising. An incoming CEO buying with full knowledge of the quarter to date into his first print is weak evidence against a kitchen-sink reset.
findings.independence: None. The source is one secondary report of the Form 4, and the Form 4 itself was not fetched.

findings.finding: This is the first print under CEO Lyons, who came from PNC. The CFO said the strategy evaluation that began earlier in the year now has 'a lot of urgency and intensity', and RBC's Gerard Cassidy expects more divestitures. Exits from marine/RV and RAC have already been made. New targets (the current target is 16-18% ROTCE over 3-5 years and 15% for 2027) or more exits or charges could come with this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior CEO-transition print in the baseline. The 2025-01-17 print that gave a new-year guide moved +5.94%, the largest of the seven.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is unknowable before the call, so this finding sits at 0 and works through abs_move_pct. The 6.14% implied move suggests the option market is pricing exactly this uncertainty.
findings.independence: American Banker 2026-09-15 on the RAC exit as the first step of Lyons's 'fewer businesses' strategy (https://www.americanbanker.com/news/under-new-ceo-truist-is-exiting-near-prime-auto-lending).

findings.finding: Peer fee read for Q3 is mixed. Capital-markets fees were strong at USB (+69% y/y including BTIG), Goldman equities and Citi IB, while JPMorgan fixed-income trading was weak and PNC's fees fell 6% q/q, in line with its -5% to 5.5% guide, after a strong Q2 in capital markets. Truist guided fees flat q/q after raising its FY fee growth to ~10% in July. Zacks looks for IB and trading of about $361.5M and modest mortgage income, with mortgage rates near 7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fees were raised in Q2 (to ~10% FY growth) and the stock still fell 1.41%, so fees have not driven the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer prints this week came after Truist last spoke, but they point in different directions, so the read is weak.
findings.independence: AP/Fortune on JPM, GS, Citi and WFC on 2026-10-13 (https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/); PNC 3Q26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026065936/q32026financialhighlightsa.htm). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Peer consumer credit was benign in Q3. PNC's total delinquencies fell to 0.34% from 0.39% and NCOs were 28bp. AP reported consumers 'continue to pay their bills' across JPM, Citi and WFC, and USB's NCO ratio was 0.51%. Truist's FY NCO guide is ~55bp, and indirect auto, about a third of its nonaccruals in Q2, is being sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has not been the swing line in Truist's recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and largely expected. PNC's nonperforming loans rose 8% on office CRE and one large commercial credit, which partly offsets the benign consumer read.
findings.independence: AP/Fortune 2026-10-13 (https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/); USB 3Q26 results (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036104/000003610426000054/a3q26earningsrelease.htm). This is a proxy.

outside_window.finding: RAC layoffs run from 2026-11-30 to 2027-07-31 as locations close, and the cost savings and the NCO reduction (about 10bp a year) land in 2027. Modest 2027 EPS/ROTCE accretion per the company.

baseline_tension: The one directional finding (a peer-read and rate risk to the forward NII guide) agrees with the +7.97 put skew and the 12.6% slide since the July guide cut, so it is probably largely priced. The reaffirmation, the CEO buy and the accretive exit cut against the skew, but none is strong enough to say the option market is wrong, which leaves p_up at 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 / core table, 'lands inside what the company guided': the Q3 reaffirmation finding falls from +0.5 to +0.2 because it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect (it is now listed second, before the RAC finding).
Rule 2, one-offs: the RAC reserve recapture and securities repositioning fall from +0.4 to +0.2, sized as a one-off whose only path to the multiple is the NII pickup in the forward guide.
Rule 5, proxies filed small: the peer fee read and the peer credit read each fall from +0.2 to +0.1. The CEO insider buy falls from +0.3 to +0.2 (single secondary source, inference).

Rule 7, positioning: the negative NII-guide finding agrees with the skew and short interest is 2.3% (not crowded), so it stays at -1.0. Rule 3: its counter-argument (longer rates help asset repricing) is already reflected in its range.

Rule 6, bar: the EPS consensus is disputed ($1.05 / $1.07 / $1.13, range $0.37-1.52), so nothing is sized against EPS; revenue and NII are sized against the company guide, which counts as a sourced bar.
